kx + 93 = 7x + 15k
In the equation above, k is a constant. Ana solves the equation for each integer k from 5 to 19, inclusive, for which it has a solution. What is the difference between the greatest and the least of the solutions she finds?

A woodworker makes chairs and stools each week. Each chair uses $7 of materials and earns a profit of $13, and each stool uses $4 of materials and earns a profit of $7. The weekly materials budget is $100, and because chairs are sold in sets with stools, the woodworker makes at most 4 more chairs than stools. Only whole chairs and stools are made. What is the greatest possible weekly profit, in dollars?

A woodshop class makes birdhouses and planter boxes to sell. Each birdhouse uses $8 of lumber, takes 2 hours to build, and earns a profit of $13. Each planter box uses $5 of lumber, takes 6 hours to build, and earns a profit of $8. The class can spend at most $159 on lumber, and the course requires the class to log at least 120 hours of building time. Only whole items are built. In the plan with the greatest total profit, what is the number of planter boxes minus the number of birdhouses?

A summer camp needs tents to sleep at least 151 campers. A large tent sleeps 9 campers and costs $44 per night, and a small tent sleeps 4 campers and costs $20 per night. Camp rules require at least twice as many small tents as large tents. Only whole tents are rented, and the camp rents the least expensive combination of tents that meets both conditions. What is the total number of tents in that combination?

A community garden is buying fruit trees and shrubs. Each fruit tree costs $63 and each shrub costs $14, and the garden can spend at most $882. The planting plan requires the number of shrubs to be at least 1.2 times the number of fruit trees. Only whole trees and shrubs are bought, and the garden wants to buy the greatest possible number of fruit trees. How many different combinations of fruit trees and shrubs include that greatest number of fruit trees?

kx + 5y = 5
x + y = 4
The system above contains the constant k. For each integer k from 0 to 20, inclusive, that gives the system exactly one solution, the y-coordinate of that solution is written down. What is the sum of the greatest and the least of the numbers written down?

A candle is 39 centimeters tall when it is lit, and it burns down at a constant rate of 20 centimeters every 4 hours. Its height is recorded when it is lit and then every hour on the hour until it burns out. A recorded height counts as a reading if it is at least 9 centimeters and less than k centimeters. Exactly 4 of the recorded heights are readings. What is the least integer value of k for which this is true?

A relief team must ship at least 488 meals on a cart that can hold at most 80 kilograms. A crate holds 28 meals, weighs 5 kilograms, and costs $54; a box holds 12 meals, weighs 1 kilogram, and costs $24. Only whole crates and boxes are shipped, and the team chooses the least expensive shipment that meets both conditions. In that shipment, by how many does the number of crates exceed the number of boxes?

In the xy-plane, line q passes through the points (4, 20) and (6, 26). Line p has equation y = kx - 4, where k is a constant. For how many integers k with -19 ≤ k ≤ 24 do lines p and q intersect at a point whose x-coordinate is less than -1 or greater than 3?

x - 20 < kx ≤ 4x + 56
In the compound inequality above, k is a constant. For how many integer values of k does the compound inequality have exactly 3 integer solutions?

The water level in a tank, in centimeters, t minutes after a valve is set is modeled by L(t) = 23 + kt, where k is an integer (k is negative if the tank is draining). The level is read once at each whole number of minutes from t = 1 through t = 12. A reading is acceptable if the level is at least 2 centimeters and less than 71 centimeters. Exactly 3 of the 12 readings are acceptable. What is the sum of all possible integer values of k?

x + 3y = 4
The two equations above share the constant k. Looking only at integers k from -19 to 47, inclusive, for how many such k is there an ordered pair (x, y) that satisfies both equations and has y < -1 or y > 4?

kx + 30 = 12x + 10k
In the equation above, k is a constant. Of the integers k from -20 to 40, inclusive, how many make the equation have a solution x with 4 ≤ x ≤ 19?

A climbing gym offers two plans. Plan A has a one-time fee of k dollars plus $12 per visit. Plan B has a one-time fee of 3k dollars plus $5 per visit. Dana will make n visits, where n is a positive whole number. She wants Plan A to cost less than Plan B, and she wants Plan A to cost at most $260 in total. For some integer values of k, exactly 6 values of n meet both of Dana's conditions. What is the difference between the greatest and least such values of k?

A bakery makes x trays of muffins and y trays of scones each morning, where x and y are whole numbers. A tray of muffins costs $7 to make and earns a profit of $10, and a tray of scones costs $4 to make and earns a profit of $6. The bakery can spend at most $101 on these trays, it wants a total profit of at least $144, and it must make at least 7 trays of muffins. How many different plans (x, y) meet all three requirements?

6x + k = 2x + 41
In the two equations above, k is the same constant. What is the sum of all values of k for which the two equations have at least one solution x in common?

A market stand sells pies and loaves of bread. Each pie costs $9 to bake and earns a profit of $16, and each loaf costs $5 to bake and earns a profit of $10. The stand can spend at most $154 on baking, and its shelf can display at most 23 items in total. Last week the stand baked 0 pies and 23 loaves. Only whole pies and loaves are baked. How much greater is the greatest possible total profit for a week than last week's total profit?

The shop has 249 milliliters of ink and 140 sheets of paper, earns a profit of $14 on each poster and $18 on each banner, and makes only whole posters and banners. In the plan with the greatest total profit, how many posters does the shop make?
